title: Inverted-hull outline with constant pixel width
purpose: Draw ink outlines around three.js meshes: a shell that shares the mesh's geometry renders only back faces, each vertex pushed along its projected normal by a fixed number of pixels in clip space, so the outline keeps its width at any distance and works on InstancedMesh. Use it for toon, comic and selection looks.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (the fragment stage includes the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

limits: Stylized. The hull follows smooth vertex normals: on hard-edged meshes with split normals the shell tears open at creases, so weld normals first (or use a smoothed normal attribute). Inner creases and intersections get no line; only silhouettes do. Width is in drawing-buffer pixels, so uResolution must follow the renderer on resize and pixel ratio changes. Skinned and morphed meshes are not followed. Each outline is a second draw call. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Clip-space vertex offset by a projected normal for a constant screen-space width
